Help

Questions, answered plainly.

These are the answers as they stand today, including the ones that are simply no.

Common questions

Can I place an order?

Yes — you can request an invoice. Add a piece to the cart and continue to checkout. OPAR confirms the price, delivery and payment method before anything is paid.

Does the cart work?

The cart stores items in this browser and survives navigation. It shares its storage with the main application. It does not take payment.

What is a partner offer?

A piece where the purchase happens with another merchant. The page says so, the button leads to their site, and OPAR may earn a commission if you buy. Price, delivery and returns are theirs.

Do you ship, and where?

OPAR is being built for international delivery. Destinations and charges are confirmed on your invoice while the shipping service is being connected.

Where are the free books and music?

In Perennis. The library is public, and titles appear as their editions and recording permissions are confirmed.

Do any products treat or cure illness?

No. OPAR does not sell medicines and does not publish treatment, prevention or cure claims. Information on this site is not medical advice; supplements can interact with medication, so speak to a qualified practitioner.

How is the price set during construction?

During construction, shop listings show construction-sample pricing alongside variants and shipping notes so cart and checkout flows can be tested. Final selling prices are confirmed on your written invoice before payment, and nothing is charged at checkout.

How do I look up my invoice request?

Visit Track order (/order/) and enter both your invoice reference and the email address used at checkout. Lookups check browser-local construction storage on your current device until a server backend connects.

Compliance & FAQ

A single register of every claim OPAR makes and the evidence behind it. A product may only be sold, and a claim may only be published, when the matching record is 'verified'. Missing evidence is recorded as missing, never implied.

01 · Supplier verification

Named makers & UK/EU Responsible Persons

Marketplace listings frequently mask who actually manufactures an item. OPAR traces beyond reseller storefronts to the factory name, country of origin, and statutory Responsible Person—explicitly recording gaps such as malformed EU addresses or missing Great Britain representatives.

02 · INCI ingredient listings

Ordered declarations over marketing blurbs

Marketing highlights ("with tea tree oil and aloe") are not accepted as cosmetic ingredient disclosures. Regulated soaps and topicals require complete weight-ordered INCI lists; botanical supplements require per-serving Supplement Facts kept distinct from gross shipping weight and conflicting feed attributes.

03 · Safety reports & lab COAs

Cosmetic CPSRs & batch Certificates of Analysis

Topical cosmetics require a Cosmetic Product Safety Report (CPSR) and microbiological / heavy-metal testing prior to sale. Ingestible botanicals require a batch-specific third-party COA. Packaging PDF artwork or supplier badges are never treated as safety verification or organic certification.

Verification questions answered

Detailed Compliance & Verification FAQ

How does OPAR verify suppliers and manufacturers?

OPAR traces beyond marketplace storefront names to confirm the legal manufacturer identity, facility country of origin, and applicable Responsible Person appointments (keeping EU and Great Britain / UK appointments separate). Where a listing cites an EU representative with a malformed address or lacks a UK Responsible Person, the gap stays visible in the product Verification File and live trading remains closed.

How does OPAR handle INCI ingredient listings and Supplement Facts?

For cosmetic soaps and topical items, marketing ingredient highlights (such as naming niacinamide, tea tree oil, or aloe without concentration order) are never treated as a valid declaration. OPAR requires a complete, weight-ordered INCI list before opening live sales. For ingestible botanicals, label artwork figures—such as capsule count and per-serving botanical mass—are recorded explicitly as label-stated and separated from gross parcel weight or conflicting marketplace category tags.

How does OPAR manage cosmetic safety reports (CPSRs) and batch laboratory testing?

Cosmetics intended for UK or EU customers require a Cosmetic Product Safety Report (CPSR), batch-code inspection, and microbiological and heavy-metal testing. Botanical supplements require batch-specific third-party Certificates of Analysis (COAs) covering botanical identity, active amounts, microbiology, and contaminants. Every missing report is logged as not-provided or pending in OPAR's public register rather than hidden.

Does supplier label artwork or a marketplace badge count as organic or safety certification?

No. A one-page label PDF proves what is printed on packaging artwork; it is not an organic certificate, allergen guarantee, or laboratory test report. OPAR strips unverified supplier phrases—including anti-acne, skin lightening, organic certification, or clinically proven claims—and logs them under excluded supplier wording on each product page.

Why are preview items with 0 verified safety checks visible in the Shop?

During pre-launch construction, OPAR publishes selected previews alongside their exact verification score (for example, 0 of 9 checks verified) and keeps card checkout disabled. Customers can inspect the honest evidence ledger, compare rooms, and test the written-invoice inquiry workflow without any payment credential collection.

How do partner offers differ from OPAR shop compliance?

Partner offers (marked Discover / Partner offer) are sold and fulfilled on external merchants' websites, where the merchant holds seller obligations for pricing, shipping, and product compliance. Even there, OPAR withholds unverified efficacy, price, or stock claims from its introductory copy.
